record.paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
record.original_question: For optimal controls of stochastic distributed parameter systems, can one establish higher-order necessary conditions under weaker assumptions than those used in the existing literature, potentially by first proving the existence of a transposition solution to the second adjoint equation (3.7)?

evidence.quote: Q is used to get higher-order necessary conditions and to solve operator-valued backward stochastic Riccati equations ...

(9) Higher-order necessary conditions for optimal controls. Similar to calculus, in addition to the first-order necessary conditions (PMP), sometimes higher-order necessary conditions should be established to distinguish optimal controls from the candidates satisfying the first-order necessary conditions trivially. Some results in this direction for SDPSs can be found in [12, 13, 32]. However, these results were obtained only under very strong assumptions which should be relaxed. To this end, we believe one should first show the existence of a transposition solution to equation (3.7).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\{\mathcal F_t\}_{t\in[0,T]},\mathbb P)$ be a complete filtered probability space carrying a one-dimensional standard Brownian motion $W$. Let $H$ and $U$ be separable Hilbert spaces, $U_{ad}\subset U$ a nonempty (not necessarily convex) set of admissible control values, and let $A:\mathcal D(A)\subset H\to H$ generate a $C_0$-semigroup on $H$. Consider the controlled stochastic evolution equation
$$dx(t)=\bigl(Ax(t)+a(t,x(t),u(t))\bigr)\,dt+b(t,x(t),u(t))\,dW(t),\qquad x(0)=x_0\in H,$$
with cost functional
$$J(u(\cdot))=\mathbb E\Bigl[\int_0^T f(t,x(t),u(t))\,dt+g(x(T))\Bigr],$$
where $a,b,f,g$ are suitably measurable maps that are twice Fréchet differentiable in the state variable with locally bounded derivatives. Admissible controls $u(\cdot)$ are $\{\mathcal F_t\}$-adapted processes valued in $U_{ad}$.

Let $\bar u(\cdot)$ be an optimal control with corresponding state $\bar x(\cdot)$. The first-order adjoint equation is a vector-valued backward stochastic evolution equation in $H$. The second-order adjoint equation has the form
$$dP(t)=-\bigl(A^* P(t)+P(t)A+\mathbb H_{xx}(t,\bar x(t),\bar u(t),P(t),\cdots)\bigr)\,dt+Q(t)\,dW(t),\qquad P(T)=g_{xx}(\bar x(T)),\qquad (\star)$$
an operator-valued backward stochastic evolution equation for the pair $(P,Q)$ of $\mathcal L(H)$-valued adapted processes, where $\mathbb H$ denotes the associated Hamiltonian. A transposition solution to $(\star)$ is a pair $(P,Q)$ defined by duality against test processes through an integration-by-parts identity, rather than as a strong or mild solution.

Problem. Under assumptions on $A$, $U_{ad}$, and on $a,b,f,g$ that are strictly weaker than those currently available in the literature on higher-order optimality for such infinite-dimensional stochastic control problems (in particular, without requiring strong regularity or compactness hypotheses on $A$ or on the coefficients beyond standard measurability and twice differentiability with locally bounded derivatives):

(a) Establish the existence (and appropriate uniqueness) of a transposition solution $(P,Q)$ to the operator-valued backward stochastic evolution equation $(\star)$.

(b) Using (a), derive higher-order (in particular, second-order) necessary optimality conditions that any optimal control $\bar u(\cdot)$ must satisfy, refining the first-order Pontryagin-type maximum principle.
artifact.category_tag: Stochastic optimal control in infinite dimensions
artifact.status_search_result: Second-order necessary conditions for stochastic optimal control problems of stochastic evolution equations have been established using transposition / relaxed-transposition solutions of operator-valued backward stochastic evolution equations (Lü–Zhang, Frankowska–Zhang–Zhang, and a 2024/2025 work on "Properties for transposition solutions to operator-valued BSEEs and applications to robust second order necessary conditions"). These yield higher-order necessary conditions, but typically under fairly strong assumptions. Relaxing these assumptions and obtaining existence of genuine (not only relaxed) transposition solutions to the second adjoint equation in full generality remains an active line of research and is not fully resolved.
